title: Upcoming IPOs, Explained Simply — October 2026
description: This week, you can learn about IPOs from Vishal Nirmiti Limited, Nityas Gems and Jewellery Limited, Eventions Limited, SMC Global Securities Limited, and R.K.

faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Applications Supported by Blocked Amount) facility or through your stockbroker's online platform. Your money remains in your bank account until shares are allotted.
A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must bid for in an IPO. You cannot buy individual shares; you must apply in multiples of the specified lot.

faq.q: What is a Mainboard IPO vs. an SME IPO?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies that list on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE). SME IPOs are for smaller companies that list on dedicated SME platforms of these exchanges, often with different regulations and minimum investment amounts.

faq.q: Can I apply for multiple lots?
faq.a: Yes, you can apply for multiple lots. However, as a retail investor, your total application value cannot exceed ₹2 lakhs. For applications above ₹2 lakhs, you fall into the HNI/NII category.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get an allotment?
faq.a: If you don't receive an allotment of shares, the money that was blocked in your bank account for the IPO application will be unblocked or refunded to you.
